Albania / Baked main

Tave Kosi

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 10 minutes

This original Albania home-style baked main centers on lamb with rice, seasoned with yogurt, mint, and black pepper. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 500 g lamb
  • 180 g rice
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of yogurt, mint, and black pepper
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the lamb lightly with the onion, then add the rice and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Serve after a short rest so the tray sets and the juices settle.

Albania / Skillet main

Fergese e Tiranes

Yield
4 servings
Time
35 minutes

This original Albania home-style skillet main centers on peppers with brined cheese, seasoned with tomato, paprika, and garlic. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 6 medium peppers
  • 160 g brined cheese
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 2 tomatoes, chopped
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of tomato, paprika, and garlic
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the fat in a wide pan and soften the onion.
  2. Add the peppers and the brined cheese, and cook until the mixture starts to concentrate.
  3. Season with tomato, paprika, and garlic and cook until the pan looks glossy and thick.
  4. If eggs or cheese belong in the dish, fold them through right at the end.
  5. Serve straight from the pan with bread.

Bring the whole pan to the table with bread for scooping.

Albania / Savory pie

Byrek me Spinaq

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

This original Albania home-style savory pie centers on spinach with brined cheese, seasoned with dill and yogurt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g spinach
  • 180 g brined cheese
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of dill and yogurt
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the spinach until softened, then fold in the brined cheese and the dill and yogurt.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of lemon.

Albania / Bean stew

Jani me Fasule

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 15 minutes

This original Albania home-style bean stew centers on white beans with tomatoes, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and parsley. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 300 g cooked or 180 g dried white beans
  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 2 tomatoes, chopped
  • 700 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of paprika, garlic, and parsley
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Brown the onion in fat until golden.
  2. Add the white beans and cook until it picks up some color.
  3. Stir in the tomatoes, tomatoes, and paprika, garlic, and parsley.
  4. Add the stock, cover, and simmer slowly until rich and tender.
  5. Adjust salt, reduce the sauce if needed, and serve with bread or a spoon of yogurt.

Serve with bread, polenta, or a sharp salad.

Albania / Stuffed main

Speca te Mbushur

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 20 minutes

This original Albania home-style stuffed main centers on sweet peppers with rice, seasoned with beef, mint, and tomato. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 8 medium sweet peppers
  • 180 g rice
  • 250 g minced meat or chopped mushrooms
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 2 tomatoes, grated
  • 500 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of beef, mint, and tomato
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Prepare the vegetables or leaves so they are ready to fill.
  2. Cook the onion with the rice and mix in the minced meat or mushrooms, then season with beef, mint, and tomato.
  3. Fill the sweet peppers loosely and arrange them snugly in a pot or tray.
  4. Add grated tomato, stock, and oil, then cover and cook until the filling is tender.
  5. Rest briefly before serving so the parcels hold together.

Serve with pan juices and a spoon of yogurt or sour cream.

Albania / Grilled meat

Qofte Shtepie

Yield
4 to 6 servings
Time
45 minutes

This original Albania home-style grilled meat centers on beef and lamb mince with onion, seasoned with garlic, parsley, and paprika. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 500 g beef and lamb mince
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of garlic, parsley, and paprika
  • salt and black pepper
  • flatbread or raw onion for serving

Method

  1. Combine the beef and lamb mince, the onion, garlic, and the seasoning blend.
  2. Mix well and let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
  3. Shape into skewers, patties, or small logs depending on the dish.
  4. Grill or sear over high heat until browned outside and juicy inside.
  5. Serve immediately with flatbread, onion, and something cool on the side.

Serve with flatbread, onion, and a cool salad or relish.

Albania / Fried bread

Petulla

Yield
16 to 20 pieces
Time
45 minutes

This original Albania home-style fried bread centers on yogurt with fresh cheese, seasoned with olive oil and sea salt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 350 g flour
  • 1 tsp yeast or baking powder
  • 200 ml warm liquid
  • 250 g or ml yogurt
  • 100 g fresh cheese
  • oil for frying
  • 1 tsp olive oil and sea salt
  • pinch of salt

Method

  1. Mix the dough ingredients into a soft, slightly sticky dough or batter.
  2. Fold in the yogurt, the fresh cheese, and the flavoring, then rest for 15 to 20 minutes.
  3. Heat a few centimeters of oil in a pan.
  4. Drop or shape portions into the oil and fry until puffed and deeply golden.
  5. Drain well and finish with the sweet or savory garnish that suits the dish.

Best eaten warm, either dusted with sugar or paired with cheese.

Albania / Milk cake

Trilece

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Albania home-style milk cake centers on milk with cream, seasoned with caramel and vanilla. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 250 g or ml milk
  • 250 g or ml cream
  • 80 g melted butter or oil
  • 1 tbsp caramel and vanilla
  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.
  2. Whisk the sugar and eggs, then add the liquid and melted butter.
  3. Fold in the flour, the milk, the cream, and the flavoring.
  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.
  5. Cool slightly before slicing, adding syrup if the cake style calls for it.

Serve with coffee, tea, or a small glass of dessert wine.

Albania / Butter cookie

Ballokume

Yield
24 pieces
Time
45 minutes

This original Albania home-style butter cookie centers on cornmeal with butter, seasoned with orange zest and sugar. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 280 g flour
  • 120 g butter
  • 100 g sugar
  • 250 g cornmeal
  • 80 g butter
  • 1 egg
  • 1 tsp orange zest and sugar
  • pinch of salt

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line a tray.
  2. Cream the butter and sugar, then add the egg.
  3. Fold in the flour with the cornmeal, the butter, and the flavoring.
  4. Shape into small portions and bake until just golden at the edges.
  5. Cool before storing or finishing with syrup or jam.

Store in a tin and serve with coffee or tea.

Albania / Flatbread

Korca Herb Flatbread

Yield
1 loaf or tray
Time
1 hour 30 minutes

This original Albania home-style flatbread centers on herbs with yogurt, seasoned with dill, butter, and sea salt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 400 g flour or cornmeal
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1 tsp yeast or baking powder
  • 250 ml warm liquid
  • 180 g herbs
  • 250 g or ml yogurt
  • 2 tbsp butter or oil
  • 1 tsp dill, butter, and sea salt

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and grease a loaf tin or tray.
  2. Combine the dry ingredients, then stir in the warm liquid and fat.
  3. Fold in the herbs, the yogurt, and the flavoring until you have a thick batter or soft dough.
  4. Spread or shape the dough in the pan.
  5. Bake until the loaf is golden and sounds hollow when tapped.

Serve warm from the oven or toasted the next day.

Albania / Soup

Berat Lentil And Tomato Soup

Yield
6 servings
Time
55 minutes

This original Albania home-style soup centers on lentils with tomatoes, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and oregano. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 300 g cooked or 180 g dried lentils
  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tbsp chopped seasoning mix of paprika, garlic, and oregano
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.
  2. Add the lentils, the tomatoes, and paprika, and stir for 2 minutes.
  3. Pour in the stock and simmer gently until the main ingredient is tender.
  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.
  5. Serve hot with bread and a final spoon of olive oil.

Serve with crusty bread and a final drizzle of olive oil.

This original Albania home-style soup centers on chicken with onion, seasoned with oregano, garlic, and black pepper. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 500 g chicken
  • 1 large onion
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tbsp chopped seasoning mix of oregano, garlic, and black pepper
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.
  2. Add the chicken, the onion, and paprika, and stir for 2 minutes.
  3. Pour in the stock and simmer gently until the main ingredient is tender.
  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.
  5. Serve hot with bread and a final spoon of olive oil.

Serve with crusty bread and a final drizzle of olive oil.

Albania / Cake

Tirana Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Albania home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, brined cheese, yogurt, mint, peppers, and lamb.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil
  • 1 tbsp vanilla and citrus zest
  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.
  2. Whisk the sugar and eggs, then add the liquid and melted butter.
  3. Fold in the flour, the honey, the walnut, and the flavoring.
  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.
  5. Cool slightly before slicing, adding syrup if the cake style calls for it.

Serve with coffee, tea, or a small glass of dessert wine.

Bosnia and Herzegovina / Grilled meat

Cevapi

Yield
4 to 6 servings
Time
45 minutes

This original Bosnia and Herzegovina home-style grilled meat centers on beef and lamb mince with onion, seasoned with garlic, paprika, and black pepper. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beef, lamb, peppers, yogurt sauces, and slow-cooked broths.

Ingredients

  • 500 g beef and lamb mince
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of garlic, paprika, and black pepper
  • salt and black pepper
  • flatbread or raw onion for serving

Method

  1. Combine the beef and lamb mince, the onion, garlic, and the seasoning blend.
  2. Mix well and let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
  3. Shape into skewers, patties, or small logs depending on the dish.
  4. Grill or sear over high heat until browned outside and juicy inside.
  5. Serve immediately with flatbread, onion, and something cool on the side.

Serve with flatbread, onion, and a cool salad or relish.

Burek

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 500 g beef mince
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of paprika and parsley
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the beef mince until softened, then fold in the onion and the paprika and parsley.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of vinegar.

  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 500 g chicken
  • 300 g okra
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tbsp chopped seasoning mix of root vegetables and parsley
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.

  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.

1 hour

This original Bosnia and Herzegovina home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beef, lamb, peppers, yogurt sauces, and slow-cooked broths.

  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut

Method

Bulgaria / Savory pie

Banitsa

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

This original Bulgaria home-style savory pie centers on phyllo dough with sirene cheese, seasoned with eggs and yogurt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of sirene cheese, peppers, yogurt, mint, and hearty clay pot dishes.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 8 sheets phyllo dough
  • 180 g sirene cheese
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of eggs and yogurt
  • salt and black pepper

Method

Time
1 hour

This original Bulgaria home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of sirene cheese, peppers, yogurt, mint, and hearty clay pot dishes.

Ingredients

  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut

Method

Croatia / Savory pie

Soparnik

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

This original Croatia home-style savory pie centers on chard with onion, seasoned with olive oil and garlic. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, Adriatic fish, chard, cured meats, and slow braises.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g chard
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of olive oil and garlic
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the chard until softened, then fold in the onion and the olive oil and garlic.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of lemon.

Croatia / Cake

Zagreb Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Croatia home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, Adriatic fish, chard, cured meats, and slow braises.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil

  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.

  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.

Yield

Time
1 hour 10 minutes

This original Greece home-style baked main centers on eggplant with potatoes, seasoned with beef, cinnamon, and bechamel. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, lemon, oregano, feta, vegetables, and island-style sweets.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 300 g eggplant
  • 400 g potatoes
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of beef, cinnamon, and bechamel
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the eggplant lightly with the onion, then add the potatoes and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.

Time
1 hour

This original Greece home-style savory pie centers on spinach with feta, seasoned with dill and olive oil. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, lemon, oregano, feta, vegetables, and island-style sweets.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough

  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g spinach
  • 180 g feta
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of dill and olive oil
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the spinach until softened, then fold in the feta and the dill and olive oil.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of lemon.

Greece / Soup

Thessaly Lentil And Tomato Soup

Yield
6 servings
Time
55 minutes

This original Greece home-style soup centers on lentils with tomatoes, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and dill. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, lemon, oregano, feta, vegetables, and island-style sweets.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 300 g cooked or 180 g dried lentils
  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tbsp chopped seasoning mix of paprika, garlic, and dill
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.

  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.
  5. Serve hot with bread and a final spoon of olive oil.

Greece / Cake

Athens Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Greece home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, lemon, oregano, feta, vegetables, and island-style sweets.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil
  • 1 tbsp vanilla and citrus zest
  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.

  3. Fold in the flour, the honey, the walnut, and the flavoring.
  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.
  5. Cool slightly before slicing, adding syrup if the cake style calls for it.

Serve with coffee, tea, or a small glass of dessert wine.

Kosovo / Layered bake

Flija

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 10 minutes

This original Kosovo home-style layered bake centers on cream with butter, seasoned with yogurt and layered batter. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of lamb, dairy, peppers, layered breads, and family-style tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 250 g or ml cream
  • 200 g butter
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of yogurt and layered batter
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the cream lightly with the onion, then add the butter and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Serve after a short rest so the tray sets and the juices settle.

Kosovo / Savory pie

Pite me Spinaq

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

This original Kosovo home-style savory pie centers on spinach with brined cheese, seasoned with dill and black pepper. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of lamb, dairy, peppers, layered breads, and family-style tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g spinach
  • 180 g brined cheese
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of dill and black pepper
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the spinach until softened, then fold in the brined cheese and the dill and black pepper.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of lemon.

Kosovo / Soup

Peja Lentil And Tomato Soup

6 servings

55 minutes

This original Kosovo home-style soup centers on lentils with tomatoes, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and parsley. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of lamb, dairy, peppers, layered breads, and family-style tray bakes.

  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika

Method

Kosovo / Cake

Prizren Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Kosovo home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of lamb, dairy, peppers, layered breads, and family-style tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut

Method

Montenegro / Hearty porridge

Kacamak

Yield
4 servings
Time
35 minutes

This original Montenegro home-style hearty porridge centers on potatoes with kajmak, seasoned with cornmeal, butter, and cheese. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of mountain dairy, lamb, smoked meat, cornmeal, and coastal frying.

Ingredients

  • 220 g cornmeal, flour, or cooked beans
  • 700 ml water or milk
  • 400 g potatoes
  • 250 g or ml kajmak
  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 1 tbsp cornmeal, butter, and cheese
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Bring the liquid to a simmer in a heavy pot.
  2. Whisk in the meal or bean base so it thickens without lumps.
  3. Fold in the potatoes, the kajmak, and the flavoring.
  4. Cook on low heat until the porridge is thick, silky, and rich.
  5. Serve hot with extra butter, cheese, or yogurt.

Serve hot with extra cheese, yogurt, or butter on top.

Method

Montenegro / Savory pie

This original Montenegro home-style savory pie centers on spinach with fresh cheese, seasoned with parsley and yogurt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of mountain dairy, lamb, smoked meat, cornmeal, and coastal frying.

Ingredients

  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g spinach
  • 180 g fresh cheese
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of parsley and yogurt

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.

  • 1 large onion, finely chopped

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.

Montenegro / Soup

Njegusi Lentil And Tomato Soup

Yield
6 servings
Time
55 minutes

This original Montenegro home-style soup centers on lentils with tomatoes, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and mint. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of mountain dairy, lamb, smoked meat, cornmeal, and coastal frying.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 300 g cooked or 180 g dried lentils
  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tbsp chopped seasoning mix of paprika, garlic, and mint
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.

  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.
  5. Serve hot with bread and a final spoon of olive oil.

  • 1 large onion, sliced

Method

North Macedonia / Baked beans

Tavce Gravce

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 10 minutes

This original North Macedonia home-style baked beans centers on white beans with onion, seasoned with paprika, mint, and dried pepper. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, peppers, yogurt, grilled meats, and bright paprika.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 300 g cooked or 180 g dried white beans
  • 1 large onion
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of paprika, mint, and dried pepper
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the white beans lightly with the onion, then add the onion and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Serve after a short rest so the tray sets and the juices settle.

North Macedonia / Open pie

Pastrmajlija

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

This original North Macedonia home-style open pie centers on bread dough with beef or lamb, seasoned with paprika and black pepper. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, peppers, yogurt, grilled meats, and bright paprika.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 500 g bread dough
  • 500 g beef or lamb
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of paprika and black pepper
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the bread dough until softened, then fold in the beef or lamb and the paprika and black pepper.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of vinegar.

This original North Macedonia home-style savory pie centers on pumpkin with onion, seasoned with cinnamon, black pepper, and savory. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, peppers, yogurt, grilled meats, and bright paprika.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g pumpkin
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of cinnamon, black pepper, and savory
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the pumpkin until softened, then fold in the onion and the cinnamon, black pepper, and savory.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of vinegar.

North Macedonia / Baked main

Ohrid Yogurt-Baked Chicken

Yield

Time
1 hour 10 minutes

This original North Macedonia home-style baked main centers on chicken with yogurt, seasoned with garlic, paprika, and parsley. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, peppers, yogurt, grilled meats, and bright paprika.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 500 g chicken
  • 250 g or ml yogurt
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of garlic, paprika, and parsley
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the chicken lightly with the onion, then add the yogurt and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Serve after a short rest so the tray sets and the juices settle.

North Macedonia / Cake

Skopje Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original North Macedonia home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, peppers, yogurt, grilled meats, and bright paprika.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil
  • 1 tbsp vanilla and citrus zest
  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.
  2. Whisk the sugar and eggs, then add the liquid and melted butter.
  3. Fold in the flour, the honey, the walnut, and the flavoring.
  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.
  5. Cool slightly before slicing, adding syrup if the cake style calls for it.

Serve with coffee, tea, or a small glass of dessert wine.

Romania / Stuffed main

Sarmale

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 20 minutes

This original Romania home-style stuffed main centers on cabbage leaves with rice, seasoned with pork, dill, and tomato. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of sour soups, cornmeal, roasted peppers, pork, and nut-rich baking.

Ingredients

  • 16 prepared cabbage leaves
  • 180 g rice
  • 250 g minced meat or chopped mushrooms
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 2 tomatoes, grated
  • 500 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of pork, dill, and tomato
  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Prepare the vegetables or leaves so they are ready to fill.
  2. Cook the onion with the rice and mix in the minced meat or mushrooms, then season with pork, dill, and tomato.
  3. Fill the cabbage leaves loosely and arrange them snugly in a pot or tray.
  4. Add grated tomato, stock, and oil, then cover and cook until the filling is tender.
  5. Rest briefly before serving so the parcels hold together.

Serve with pan juices and a spoon of yogurt or sour cream.

Romania / Soup

Ciorba de Burta

Yield
6 servings
Time
55 minutes

This original Romania home-style soup centers on tripe with sour cream, seasoned with garlic, vinegar, and carrot. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of sour soups, cornmeal, roasted peppers, pork, and nut-rich baking.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 500 g tripe
  • 250 g or ml sour cream
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tbsp chopped seasoning mix of garlic, vinegar, and carrot
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.
  2. Add the tripe, the sour cream, and paprika, and stir for 2 minutes.
  3. Pour in the stock and simmer gently until the main ingredient is tender.
  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.
  5. Serve hot with bread and a final spoon of sunflower oil.

Serve with crusty bread and a final drizzle of sunflower oil.

This original Romania home-style savory pie centers on spinach with brined cheese, seasoned with lovage and yogurt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of sour soups, cornmeal, roasted peppers, pork, and nut-rich baking.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g spinach
  • 180 g brined cheese

Method

  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.

Romania / Cake

Transylvanian Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Romania home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of sour soups, cornmeal, roasted peppers, pork, and nut-rich baking.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil

Method

  • 80 g sugar
  • 2 eggs
  • 80 g butter
  • 120 g hazelnut
  • 250 g or ml milk
  • 1 tbsp citrus zest, vanilla, and butter

Method

  1. Mix the dough and knead until smooth, then let it rise until doubled.
  2. Work in the hazelnut, the milk, and the flavoring.
  3. Shape into a braid or loaf and let it rise again.
  4. Brush with egg and bake until deeply golden.
  5. Cool before slicing so the crumb sets properly.

Slice once cool and serve plain or with extra jam.

Serbia / Stuffed main

Sarma

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 20 minutes

This original Serbia home-style stuffed main centers on cabbage leaves with rice, seasoned with beef, pork, and paprika. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, grilled meat, paprika, corn breads, and robust tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 16 prepared cabbage leaves
  • 180 g rice
  • 250 g minced meat or chopped mushrooms
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 2 tomatoes, grated
  • 500 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of beef, pork, and paprika
  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Prepare the vegetables or leaves so they are ready to fill.
  2. Cook the onion with the rice and mix in the minced meat or mushrooms, then season with beef, pork, and paprika.
  3. Fill the cabbage leaves loosely and arrange them snugly in a pot or tray.
  4. Add grated tomato, stock, and oil, then cover and cook until the filling is tender.
  5. Rest briefly before serving so the parcels hold together.

Serve with pan juices and a spoon of yogurt or sour cream.

Serbia / Grilled meat

Cevapi

Yield
4 to 6 servings
Time
45 minutes

This original Serbia home-style grilled meat centers on beef mince with onion, seasoned with garlic, paprika, and kajmak. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, grilled meat, paprika, corn breads, and robust tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 500 g beef mince
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of garlic, paprika, and kajmak
  • salt and black pepper
  • flatbread or raw onion for serving

Method

  1. Combine the beef mince, the onion, garlic, and the seasoning blend.
  2. Mix well and let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
  3. Shape into skewers, patties, or small logs depending on the dish.
  4. Grill or sear over high heat until browned outside and juicy inside.
  5. Serve immediately with flatbread, onion, and something cool on the side.

Serve with flatbread, onion, and a cool salad or relish.

Serbia / Baked main

Karadjordjeva Snicla

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 10 minutes

This original Serbia home-style baked main centers on veal or pork with kajmak, seasoned with breadcrumbs, lemon, and parsley. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, grilled meat, paprika, corn breads, and robust tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 500 g veal or pork
  • 250 g or ml kajmak
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of breadcrumbs, lemon, and parsley
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the veal or pork lightly with the onion, then add the kajmak and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Serve after a short rest so the tray sets and the juices settle.

Serbia / Savory pie

Gibanica

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

This original Serbia home-style savory pie centers on phyllo dough with white cheese, seasoned with eggs, yogurt, and butter. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, grilled meat, paprika, corn breads, and robust tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp sunflower oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 8 sheets phyllo dough
  • 180 g white cheese
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of eggs, yogurt, and butter
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the phyllo dough until softened, then fold in the white cheese and the eggs, yogurt, and butter.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of vinegar.

This original Serbia home-style soup centers on river fish with tomatoes, seasoned with paprika, celery, and garlic. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, grilled meat, paprika, corn breads, and robust tray bakes.

  • 600 g river fish
  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika

  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.

  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.
  5. Serve hot with bread and a final spoon of sunflower oil.

This original Serbia home-style corn bread centers on white cheese with yogurt, seasoned with cornmeal and butter. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, grilled meat, paprika, corn breads, and robust tray bakes.

  • 1 tsp yeast or baking powder

Serbia / Cake

Belgrade Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Serbia home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, grilled meat, paprika, corn breads, and robust tray bakes.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil
  • 1 tbsp vanilla and citrus zest
  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.
  2. Whisk the sugar and eggs, then add the liquid and melted butter.
  3. Fold in the flour, the honey, the walnut, and the flavoring.
  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.
  5. Cool slightly before slicing, adding syrup if the cake style calls for it.

Serve with coffee, tea, or a small glass of dessert wine.

Slovenia / Soup

Jota

Yield
6 servings
Time
55 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style soup centers on beans with sauerkraut, seasoned with potatoes, garlic, and bay leaf. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp pumpkin seed oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 300 g cooked or 180 g dried beans
  • 300 g sauerkraut
  • 1.2 liters stock or water
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tbsp chopped seasoning mix of potatoes, garlic, and bay leaf
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Warm the fat in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until fragrant.
  2. Add the beans, the sauerkraut, and paprika, and stir for 2 minutes.
  3. Pour in the stock and simmer gently until the main ingredient is tender.
  4. Taste, crush a little of the soup to thicken it if desired, and add the seasoning blend.
  5. Serve hot with bread and a final spoon of pumpkin seed oil.

Serve with crusty bread and a final drizzle of pumpkin seed oil.

Yield
8 to 10 slices
Time
2 hours

This original Slovenia home-style rolled pastry centers on walnuts with honey, seasoned with sweet dough and cinnamon. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 350 g flour
  • 7 g yeast
  • 150 ml warm milk or water
  • 60 g butter
  • 80 g walnuts
  • 120 g honey
  • 1 egg for brushing
  • 1 tbsp sweet dough and cinnamon

Method

  1. Prepare the enriched dough and let it rise once.
  2. Spread the filling made from the walnuts, the honey, and the flavoring across the dough.
  3. Roll tightly, place in the pan, and let it proof again.
  4. Bake until golden and fragrant.
  5. Cool enough to slice cleanly.

Slice after a short cooling period so the swirl holds.

Slovenia / Savory pie

Ljubljana Spinach And Fresh Cheese Pie

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour

This original Slovenia home-style savory pie centers on spinach with fresh cheese, seasoned with chives and yogurt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough
  • 3 tbsp pumpkin seed oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g spinach
  • 180 g fresh cheese
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of chives and yogurt
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.
  2. Cook the onion with the spinach until softened, then fold in the fresh cheese and the chives and yogurt.
  3. Whisk the eggs and yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a loose binding mixture.
  4. Layer the dough with oil, spoon the filling between layers, and finish with the yogurt mixture over the top.
  5. Bake until bronzed and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Serve warm with a spoon of yogurt and wedges of vinegar.

Slovenia / Baked main

Karst Yogurt-Baked Chicken

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 10 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style baked main centers on chicken with yogurt, seasoned with garlic, paprika, and parsley. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp pumpkin seed oil
  • 500 g chicken
  • 250 g or ml yogurt
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of garlic, paprika, and parsley
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the chicken lightly with the onion, then add the yogurt and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Serve after a short rest so the tray sets and the juices settle.

Slovenia / Stuffed main

Alpine Stuffed Peppers

Yield
6 servings
Time
1 hour 20 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style stuffed main centers on sweet peppers with rice, seasoned with beef, tomato, and caraway. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 8 medium sweet peppers
  • 180 g rice
  • 250 g minced meat or chopped mushrooms
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 2 tomatoes, grated
  • 500 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of beef, tomato, and caraway
  • 2 tbsp pumpkin seed oil
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Prepare the vegetables or leaves so they are ready to fill.
  2. Cook the onion with the rice and mix in the minced meat or mushrooms, then season with beef, tomato, and caraway.
  3. Fill the sweet peppers loosely and arrange them snugly in a pot or tray.
  4. Add grated tomato, stock, and oil, then cover and cook until the filling is tender.
  5. Rest briefly before serving so the parcels hold together.

Serve with pan juices and a spoon of yogurt or sour cream.

Slovenia / Grilled meat

Idrija Grilled Meatball Platter

Yield
4 to 6 servings
Time
45 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style grilled meat centers on lamb with onion, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and parsley. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 500 g lamb
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tbsp pumpkin seed oil
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of paprika, garlic, and parsley
  • salt and black pepper
  • flatbread or raw onion for serving

Method

  1. Combine the lamb, the onion, garlic, and the seasoning blend.

  4. Grill or sear over high heat until browned outside and juicy inside.
  5. Serve immediately with flatbread, onion, and something cool on the side.

Serve with flatbread, onion, and a cool salad or relish.

Slovenia / Relish

Karst Roasted Pepper Relish

Yield
3 cups
Time
1 hour

This original Slovenia home-style relish centers on peppers with tomatoes, seasoned with garlic, vinegar, and parsley. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 6 medium peppers
  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 1 large onion
  • 2 garlic cloves
  • 2 tbsp pumpkin seed oil
  • 1 tbsp vinegar juice or vinegar
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of garlic, vinegar, and parsley
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Roast or soften the peppers and the tomatoes until sweet and tender.
  2. Cook with onion, garlic, oil, and acid until the mixture thickens.
  3. Blend or mash to the texture you want, then season with garlic, vinegar, and parsley.
  4. Simmer briefly again to concentrate the flavor.
  5. Cool and serve as a spread or side dish.

Serve at room temperature as a spread or side dish.

Slovenia / Bean dip

Alpine Garlic Bean Mash

Yield
4 servings
Time
15 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style bean dip centers on white beans with garlic, seasoned with paprika oil and lemon. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 300 g cooked or 180 g dried white beans
  • 3 cloves garlic
  • 2 tbsp pumpkin seed oil
  • 1 tbsp vinegar juice or vinegar
  • 2 to 4 tbsp yogurt or water as needed
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of paprika oil and lemon
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Blend or mash the white beans with the garlic, oil, and a splash of acid.
  2. Thin with yogurt or water until spreadable.
  3. Fold in the seasoning blend of paprika oil and lemon.
  4. Taste for salt and chill briefly if you want a firmer texture.
  5. Serve with bread, vegetables, or grilled meat.

Serve chilled or cool with bread and raw vegetables.

Slovenia / Cake

Ljubljana Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Slovenia home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil
  • 1 tbsp vanilla and citrus zest
  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.
  2. Whisk the sugar and eggs, then add the liquid and melted butter.
  3. Fold in the flour, the honey, the walnut, and the flavoring.
  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.
  5. Cool slightly before slicing, adding syrup if the cake style calls for it.

Serve with coffee, tea, or a small glass of dessert wine.

Slovenia / Pudding

Piran Rice Pudding

Yield
6 servings
Time
40 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style pudding centers on rice with milk, seasoned with vanilla and cinnamon. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 700 ml liquid
  • 180 g rice
  • 250 g or ml milk
  • 80 g sugar
  • 1 tbsp butter
  • 1 tbsp vanilla and cinnamon

Method

  1. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer.
  2. Add the rice, the milk, sugar, and butter.
  3. Cook slowly, stirring often, until the pudding thickens and the flavors of vanilla and cinnamon come through.
  4. Spoon into bowls or a serving dish.
  5. Serve warm or chilled.

Serve warm for comfort or chilled for a firmer set.

Styria Sesame Cookies

Time
45 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style cookie centers on sesame seeds with butter, seasoned with orange zest and sugar. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Slovenia / Sweet bread

Soca Holiday Sweet Bread

Yield
1 loaf
Time
2 hours 30 minutes

This original Slovenia home-style sweet bread centers on hazelnut with milk, seasoned with citrus zest, vanilla, and butter. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of beans, sauerkraut, buckwheat, dairy, and alpine pastry traditions.

Ingredients

  • 450 g flour
  • 7 g yeast
  • 120 ml warm liquid
  • 80 g sugar
  • 2 eggs
  • 80 g butter
  • 120 g hazelnut
  • 250 g or ml milk
  • 1 tbsp citrus zest, vanilla, and butter

Method

  1. Mix the dough and knead until smooth, then let it rise until doubled.
  2. Work in the hazelnut, the milk, and the flavoring.
  3. Shape into a braid or loaf and let it rise again.
  4. Brush with egg and bake until deeply golden.
  5. Cool before slicing so the crumb sets properly.

Slice once cool and serve plain or with extra jam.

Turkey / Skillet main

Menemen

Yield
4 servings
Time
35 minutes

This original Turkey home-style skillet main centers on eggs with peppers, seasoned with tomato, olive oil, and oregano. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, peppers, bulgur, yogurt, grilled meats, and syrup sweets.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 4 large eggs
  • 6 medium peppers
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 2 tomatoes, chopped
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of tomato, olive oil, and oregano
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the fat in a wide pan and soften the onion.
  2. Add the eggs and the peppers, and cook until the mixture starts to concentrate.
  3. Season with tomato, olive oil, and oregano and cook until the pan looks glossy and thick.

This original Turkey home-style savory pie centers on spinach with white cheese, seasoned with mint and yogurt. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, peppers, bulgur, yogurt, grilled meats, and syrup sweets.

Ingredients

  • 8 sheets phyllo or 500 g thin pie dough

  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 300 g spinach
  • 180 g white cheese
  • 2 eggs
  • 200 g yogurt
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of mint and yogurt

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a baking tray.

This original Turkey home-style fish bake centers on sardines with tomatoes, seasoned with garlic, mint, and olive oil. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, peppers, bulgur, yogurt, grilled meats, and syrup sweets.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 600 g sardines
  • 400 g tomatoes
  • 1 large onion, sliced
  • 250 g tomato or yogurt sauce
  • 250 ml stock or water
  • 1 tbsp seasoning blend of garlic, mint, and olive oil
  • salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190 C.
  2. Brown the sardines lightly with the onion, then add the tomatoes and the seasoning blend.
  3. Transfer everything to a baking dish, moisten with sauce and stock, and cover loosely.
  4. Bake until the tray is bubbling and the top starts to bronze, uncovering near the end.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Serve after a short rest so the tray sets and the juices settle.

Method

Turkey / Cake

Edirne Honey Walnut Cake

Yield
8 slices
Time
1 hour

This original Turkey home-style cake centers on honey with walnut, seasoned with vanilla and citrus zest. It is written for this collection and inspired by the country's broader pantry of olive oil, peppers, bulgur, yogurt, grilled meats, and syrup sweets.

Ingredients

  • 220 g flour or semolina
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 120 ml neutral liquid
  • 160 g honey
  • 120 g walnut
  • 80 g melted butter or oil
  • 1 tbsp vanilla and citrus zest
  • 1 tsp baking powder

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180 C and line or grease a tin.
  2. Whisk the sugar and eggs, then add the liquid and melted butter.
  3. Fold in the flour, the honey, the walnut, and the flavoring.
  4. Spread into the tin and bake until the center springs back.
  5. Cool slightly before slicing, adding syrup if the cake style calls for it.

Serve with coffee, tea, or a small glass of dessert wine.

  • 80 g sugar

  • 80 g butter

Method
